svg.title: Same three requests, four ways
svg.desc: Panel A shows normal arrival order. Non-pipelined HTTP/1.1 on one connection is sequential. HTTP/1.1 with three connections is parallel but needs three setups. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 interleave pieces on one connection. Panel B illustrates lost product data: TCP holds later bytes for every HTTP/2 stream, while QUIC can deliver received reviews and delivery data without waiting for product recovery. Shared congestion control and other dependencies can still delay HTTP/3 streams.

g.text: Order of arrival, left to right. Illustrative, not a speed benchmark.
One at a time, in order
Multiplexing = many exchanges share one connection. Pieces are labelled by stream, so nothing gets mixed up.
B · One piece is lost on the network (product piece 2)
What the application actually receives, left to right
all streams wait for the resend
TCP hands data over in strict order, so reviews and delivery wait behind the missing product bytes.
Received reviews and delivery data can be delivered before the lost product data is recovered.
Streams still share bandwidth and congestion control, so other delays remain possible.
Both multiplex. HTTP/3 avoids TCP's cross-stream delivery blocking.
